content:
Amanda C: FYI — ACME Prod is getting a TON of 429s + spikes in p95 on Dedicated (us-west-2) starting ~09:15 PST. Customer called support, wants root cause and ETA. @oncall_sre can you triage?

support-bot: Ticket #INC-46291 created: https://redwood.ai/tickets/INC-46291 (priority: high, customer: ACME) :rotating_light:

leo_sre: I'm on it. Which dedicated pool are they on? any tenant ids?

Amanda C: tenant acme-corp, pool: rdw-dedicated-usw2-prod-7. Sample repro we got from them:
```bash
curl -i -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" -d '{"model":"rw-medium-v2","input":"hello"}'
> HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
> Content-Type: application/json
> {"error":"rate_limited","retry_after":30}
```

leo_sre: running quick metr query against allocator...
```
# allocator:rdw-dedicated-usw2-prod-7
active_gpus: 16/16 (100%)
pending_scale_up_requests: 12
autoscaler_lag: 135s
request_queue_depth: 240
avg_token_latency_p95: 850ms
```

priya_infra: looking at infra events — there was a scheduled maintenance window in us-west-2 this morning that drained 5 GPUs from the pool for firmware updates (started 08:40 PST). That dropped usable capacity ~31%. Autoscaler queued scale up but we hit reserved pool caps and backpressure started.

Marie (CS): ACME is on a reserved capacity contract. They're already unhappy. We need a mitigation plan and a customer-facing ETA.

leo_sre: also seeing auth proxy cascade errors when retries pile up -> auth service rate limits -> some 401s. snippet from auth logs:
```
[09:22:03] token_validator - WARN - 401 invalid_token for tenant acme-corp, req_id=abc123
[09:22:04] auth-rate-limiter - WARN - 429 token-verification-rate-limit, reqs_per_min=600
```

Josh P: Auth 401s/wrong tokens could be from retry storms. We should avoid aggressive client retries while we fix capacity. Any chance we can short-circuit clients to fallback model or degrade gracefully?

priya_infra: immediate plan I propose:
- bump dedicated pool burst from reserved spare (we have 4 GPUs in reserve in the region control plane) -> allocate +2 to rdw-dedicated-usw2-prod-7 now
- reduce autoscaler cooldown 60s -> 15s for this pool temporarily
- enable routing fallback for acme-corp to us-west-1 and mark eu-west as secondary if latency is acceptable
- apply token-proxy rate limit relaxers for a short window to reduce 401 cascades

Amanda C: ack. Please post exact commands so I can update CS and ACME.

leo_sre: CLI to bump pool allocation (run as infra-admin):
```bash
redwood infra pool update --pool rdw-dedicated-usw2-prod-7 --add-gpus 2 --reason "incident INC-46291 temporary burst"
```
Enable routing fallback for tenant (routing-admin):
```bash
curl -X POST "https://control-plane.redwood.ai/tenants/acme-corp/failover" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -d '{"primary":"us-west-2","fallback":["us-west-1"],"priority":"immediate"}'
```
Autoscaler cooldown patch (k8s patch example):
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
data:
  autoscaler.cooldown.seconds: "15"
```

infra-bot: Capacity increase request received. Change set ID: cs-78910. Estimated apply time: ~5-10m.

oncall_sre: Applying bump and routing changes now. Will monitor queues and token proxy metrics.

(8 minutes later)

oncall_sre: Changes applied: +2 GPUs allocated, cooldown -> 15s, failover active for acme-corp. Watching metrics.

Amanda C: ACME reports reductions in 429s and p95 down to ~300ms for their normal load. They still see occasional 429s but much improved. :relieved:

leo_sre: auth 401s dropped after throttling adjustments and routing. Current metrics: request_queue_depth: 40, autoscaler_lag: 12s, active_gpus: 14/14 (post-rebalance).

priya_infra: I'll schedule rollback of the cooldown changes and remove the extra GPUs once the maintenance is complete and capacity stabilizes. Also filing a follow-up to change maintenance windows to not overlap reserved pool usage for paying tenants.

Marie (CS): Telling ACME we'll follow up with a post-incident RCA and credit for the downtime. Please make RCA and timeline.

Josh P: Also add a note to product: consider per-tenant burst guarantees for reserved pools and a graceful degradation knob to avoid auth cascading.

leo_sre: agreed. I'll own the incident writeup. Reminder: we should add a test for autoscaler behaviour when maintenance reduces capacity midscale.

Amanda C: thanks team — closing interim loop with customer. Will attach logs to the ticket.

priya_infra: filing infra action items: INFRA-2234 (prevent maintenance on region with >=75% reserved committed), INFRA-2235 (improve autoscaler backpressure signals).

infra-bot: Incident INC-46291 status -> mitigated. Change set cs-78910 completed. Actions created: INFRA-2234, INFRA-2235.

leo_sre: will post full postmortem in #postmortems once we have timelines. Good catch by priya spotting maintenance overlap.

Amanda C: closing thread for now. If ACME reports regressions I'll reopen. :thumbsup:
